### Seeds on the wind, rain that roots them, and felled trees

✅ **Flower seed rides the wind** (`WindDispersal`). It used to drop within two tiles of the parent whatever the weather -- heavier behaviour than an acorn's, from the lightest thing in the world. It is why meadows were spreading slower than woods. Seed now goes downwind, heavy-tailed, and a still day still seeds, just not far.

✅ **Rain roots what is lying there.** A seed lies until it is watered, which is what makes rain something a player waits for rather than a weather texture. A rooted seed becomes a SEEDLING, not a bloom, and rooting respects the meadow's own ceiling.

✅ **Trees are off the grid.** They stood at exact tile centres, so an original forest read as a lattice -- every trunk on a perfect grid, which no wood has ever looked like. Each now stands somewhere within its own tile, deterministically, so a wood does not rearrange itself when a chunk reloads and no trunk drifts onto a tile the placement rules say is empty.

✅ **A felled tree lies where it fell** (`FelledTree`). Felling deleted the tree and sprayed items on the ground, which reads as the tree evaporating. Now the same sprite goes over on its side -- which way depends on the tree, so a cleared wood is not a row of trunks all pointing one way -- stops blocking the path, and holds all its wood until it is worked up over several cuts. A bigger tree is a bigger haul, so felling a seedling is not the same as felling an oak.

Two existing tests asserted the old behaviour (a killing blow sprays items and deletes the node); they now assert the two stages, and the drop itself is tested against the fallen trunk that produces it.

⬜ Seeds are still patch STATE rather than world entities -- they are rendered and can be rooted, but you cannot pick one up.
⬜ Bird digestion -> droppings planting what was swallowed.


### Birds eat because they are hungry, and leave droppings

✅ **Hunger** (`BirdDigestion`). Birds foraged constantly whether or not they needed to, which makes a bird a harvesting machine rather than an animal. A songbird gets through a serious fraction of its body weight daily, so it feeds through the day rather than at meals -- pinned from both sides by a test that counts meals across a day. A bird mid-peck finishes it rather than abandoning the grass the instant its crop fills.

✅ **Droppings**: the visible half of dispersal. Without one, a seed simply appears somewhere a bird happened to be and the player never sees the connection between the bird that ate the berry and the flower that comes up under the perch. Bounded, because scenery that accumulates forever is a leak with a sprite.

✅ **Removed a second clock I had just added.** I gave digestion its own gut-passage timer alongside the carry SeedEndozoochory already models as a distance -- two clocks for one thing, at wildly different scales (the carry is seconds of game time, a real gut passage is minutes). The timer never elapsed, so dispersal stopped happening entirely: every seed a bird swallowed simply stayed in it. The flyer's own tests caught it. The carry IS the passage; a test now pins that digestion does not own a passage clock, so it cannot come back.

✅ **The carry distance itself was real on paper and silently short in practice -- a bird's seed never actually travelled anywhere close to the 10-40 tiles `SeedEndozoochory.carry_distance_tiles` intends.** `AmbientFlyerMarker._step_seed_carrying` converted that tile count into a TIME budget (`carry_tiles * TILE_SIZE / speed`) and simply waited it out, on the unstated assumption that a carrying bird spends that whole time flying in a straight line. It does not: ordinary wander is anchored to a home point within a fairly tight radius (`AmbientFlyerMovement.direction_at`'s containment/pull logic), and nothing about carrying a seed ever moved that anchor, so a bird whose home stayed put could never get further than roughly that radius away regardless of how long the timer ran. Measured directly (not assumed) across 30 sampled `wander_seed`s for a sparrow: every single one capped out at ~2.48-2.50 tiles of net displacement, however large its own `carry_distance_tiles` roll actually was (one sample rolled 39.87 intended tiles and still only achieved 2.48) -- the sparrow's wander radius (40px = 2.5 tiles) almost exactly explains the ceiling. The mechanism was firing on schedule and planting a seed of the right species every time; it was just planting it a couple of tiles from the parent plant instead of 10-40, which defeats most of what bird dispersal is supposed to add over ground epizoochory (flower spread's own 3-14 tile range). Fixed with the same shape ground carriers (`EarthChunkManager._step_seed_dispersal`/`_step_squirrel_nut_caching`/`_step_grass_seed_caching`) already use -- resolve on REAL distance travelled since the carry started, not elapsed time -- plus one new thing those ground cases don't need: `SeedEndozoochory.carry_direction`, a seeded random heading blended into ordinary wander (`CARRY_STEER_WEIGHT = 0.9`, stronger than the pollinator scent-steer blend since there is no "looks scripted" cost here, only a real cost to a weak pull: a longer carry, not a short one), so a carrying bird actually has somewhere to lean toward instead of only being told when to stop. `_carried_seed_start_position`/`_carry_direction` replace the old `_carry_seconds_remaining` field outright. Pinned by `test_a_sparrows_seed_carry_reaches_the_real_dispersal_range_across_many_birds` (20 sampled wander_seeds, each asserted to reach at least `CARRY_MIN_TILES`) plus the existing single-seed test strengthened to the same real bound; `docs/concept/flora.md`'s bird-endozoochory section updated to match (was previously spec'd as a time budget, the very assumption that broke this). All 111 `test_ambient_flyer_marker.gd` tests and all 19 `test_seed_endozoochory.gd` tests green.

✅ **Correction to the entry above: "one new thing those ground cases don't need" was wrong -- ground carriers had the identical bug, just partly hidden.** The open question left standing: `EarthChunkManager`'s ground carriers already resolve on real distance travelled (never had the bird's TIME-budget bug), but they all move the carrying creature via `CreatureMarker`'s ordinary wander (`CreatureWander`), which turns out to be the SAME home-tethered containment shape `AmbientFlyerMovement` uses for birds -- same 40px/2.5-tile `WANDER_RADIUS`, same `HOME_PULL_FULL_RADIUS_FACTOR`. Measured rather than assumed either way: driving a bare `CreatureMarker` (no world/AI, pure wander only) through 30 sampled `wander_seed`s, net displacement from the pickup origin plateaued at a hard ~2.6 tiles for every single seed, regardless of what `carry_distance_tiles` intended -- 0/30 ever reached `SeedDispersal`'s 3-14 tile flower-epizoochory range, and only 11/30 (every one needing under ~2.7 tiles) reached `SeedCaching`'s shorter 1-6 tile mouse range. A real creature's OTHER movement (hunger/thirst-driven food-seeking, real `GrazerForaging` bites) is not available to a bird the same way, so it was a genuinely open question whether it already rescues ground carriers in practice -- checked by driving a real mouse through a real `EarthChunkManager` (Berlin terrain, real hunger/foraging AI) across a 900-simulated-second (15 minute) window for 30 sampled seeds each: it helps, but does not close the gap. Grass caching went from 11/30 to 21/30 resolving (the remaining 9 all needed >4.9 of the 1-6 tile range, and the slowest real rescue took 840 of the 900 seconds budgeted); flower dispersal barely moved, 0/30 to 2/30 (both of the two rescues were the smallest flower-dispersal targets sampled, 3.14 and 4.29 tiles -- every target above ~4.7 tiles, 28 of the 30, never resolved even across the full 15 simulated minutes). Fixed identically to the bird case above: `SeedDispersal`/`SeedCaching`/`SquirrelNutCaching.carry_direction` (a seeded heading, sampled at a `PixelNoise` coordinate independent of each module's own `carry_distance_tiles`) is picked at pickup time and blended into ordinary wander by `CreatureMarker._wander_step` (`CARRY_STEER_WEIGHT = 0.9`, same value and reasoning as `AmbientFlyerMarker`'s own) via a new `_leaned_toward_carry` helper -- `_wander_step` now calls `CreatureWander.direction_at` directly (rather than its `step_position` convenience) so the heading can be steered before it becomes a position delta, mirroring exactly how `AmbientFlyerMarker._process` blends its own `_carry_direction`. Three new marker fields (`carried_seed_direction`/`carried_grass_seed_direction`/`carried_nut_direction`, one per independent carry slot -- a creature can in principle be carrying on more than one at once, e.g. a mouse coat-riding a flower seed while also cheek-pouching a grass seed, so each gets its own sequential lean rather than one shared field) default to `Vector2.ZERO`, a harmless no-op for every pre-existing caller/test that only ever set the flag/origin pair. `SquirrelNutCaching` was fixed by analogy rather than separately measured broken first -- identical `CreatureWander`/`CreatureMarker` movement substrate and a similarly out-of-reach 2-9 tile range -- but is verified by the same real test as its two siblings, not merely assumed fixed. Pinned by three new integration tests, `test_a_<carrier>_reaches_the_real_range_across_many_<animals>` (mirroring `test_a_sparrows_seed_carry_reaches_the_real_dispersal_range_across_many_birds` exactly: 20 sampled `wander_seed`s each, world left null so the steering alone is proven sufficient rather than reliant on hunger/foraging luck), all 60 seed-scenarios passing in ~7s combined wall-clock -- the fix resolves fast, not just eventually. Plus new `carry_direction` unit tests in all three carrier modules (unit length, deterministic, varies independently of `carry_distance_tiles`) and a pickup-sets-a-real-direction test per carrier in `test_earth_chunk_manager.gd`. `docs/concept/flora.md`'s bird-endozoochory section (which had explicitly, incorrectly claimed ground wander was exempt) and its own "Spread by animal seed dispersal" section, plus `docs/concept/long_grass.md`'s "Two carriers" section, all corrected to match. All `test_seed_dispersal.gd` (16), `test_seed_caching.gd` (11), `test_squirrel_nut_caching.gd` (20), and `test_creature_marker.gd` (186) tests green; the pre-existing mouse-caching tests in `test_earth_chunk_manager.gd` re-run and unaffected.


### Footprints, pickable seeds, and flies that follow you

✅ **Snow is a per-tile overlay** (`SnowLayer`), so footprints can be carved out of it. A tint is one number for the whole world and cannot express "this tile is trodden and that one is not" -- which is why tracks could not exist at all before. Four depth bands, patchy at the shallow end because a dusting is snow lying in the dips with grass showing through, not a thin even wash. Walking PACKS the snow rather than clearing it: a trail reads as tracks, not as a trench dug to the soil, and only a thin cover is broken through to the ground.

Painted INCREMENTALLY. Repainting every loaded tile every frame is thousands of set_cell calls for a field that mostly has not changed -- the same shape of cost that took the frame rate down when the fast-forward first ran. The field repaints only when its depth crosses a band, which happens a handful of times a snowfall; footprints repaint only the tiles actually walked on.

✅ **Correction: "patchy at the shallow end" described an INTENT the code did not implement.** Every covered pixel was written fully OPAQUE at 45% coverage, so a dusting was near-white specks punched into holes -- a 50/50 dither of near-white at the finest grain the atlas can express, reported live as texture corruption rather than as snow. Three changes made the claim true. Per-band `BAND_ALPHA` writes a thin cover translucent, so the ground tints THROUGH it -- the only way this layer can tint toward a ground colour it cannot know, since one tile set is baked for every biome. `BAND_COVERAGE` was raised (`[0.45, 0.72, 0.92, 1.0]` → `[0.62, 0.82, 0.96, 1.0]`) so the shallow band is thin-but-continuous rather than half-missing. And both the coverage roll and the shade-grain roll now key off a `GRAIN_BLOCK = ArtResolution.DETAIL_MULTIPLIER` block rather than the raw art pixel, so the smallest snow mark is one WORLD pixel -- grain finer than a world pixel is a dither, not texture. Measured mean-alpha ladder 0.28 / 0.53 / 0.82 / 1.00 and mean whiteness×alpha 0.23 / 0.47 / 0.77 / 0.99, both strictly increasing. Pinned by `DUSTING_MAX_MEAN_ALPHA` / `FULL_COVER_MIN_MEAN_ALPHA` and by a per-pixel block-uniformity walk (`test_snow_layer.gd`, 22/22).

✅ **Fourth follow-up: each individual tile's own transition now fades through 25 real illustrated steps instead of hard-cutting between 4 procedural ones** -- closing the gap the third follow-up below named explicitly ("each INDIVIDUAL tile's own transition should visibly fade rather than hard-cut between bands -- not true today"). The user supplied a real illustrated asset (`assets/sprites/terrain/snowoverlay.png`, a 5x5 contact sheet of 25 hand/AI-illustrated coverage stages), and `SnowLayer.build_band_image` now slices+resizes a real cell from it instead of procedurally painting a mask -- `BAND_WHITENESS`/`BAND_COVERAGE`/`BAND_ALPHA`/`GRAIN_BLOCK` (the previous entry's own procedural machinery) are deleted outright, unused by anything else in the codebase (grepped first). `DEPTH_BANDS` is now `OVERLAY_COLUMNS * OVERLAY_ROWS = 25`, the sheet's own real frame count, not a hand-picked number. The sheet's real per-cell mean coverage does NOT read row-major (row 0's own rightmost cell already measures MORE covered, mean alpha 0.22, than row 1's own leftmost cell, 0.06 -- a genuine two-axis diagonal gradient) -- `OVERLAY_BAND_CELLS` maps each of the 25 depth bands to its sheet cell in real MEASURED ascending-coverage order (mean alpha of all 25 real cropped cells, sorted; confirmed strictly monotonic, no ties) rather than assumed reading order, which a naive row-major read would have gotten wrong (band 5 would have been LESS covered than band 4, breaking `band_for`'s core contract). The sheet's own row dividers are NOT an even grid either (measured directly: the row0/row1 divider line centers ~9px earlier than a naive 1086/5 split would put it, row3/row4's ~38px earlier) -- `OVERLAY_ROW_BANDS`/`OVERLAY_COLUMN_BANDS` are real measured pixel ranges, same "measured directly against the real PNG" convention `IllustratedTerrainSprite`'s own row_bands already use, each cropped to a centered SQUARE (the source cells are landscape rectangles) so illustrated patch shapes aren't stretched. Downscaled with **Lanczos, not nearest-neighbour**, despite nearest-neighbour being this codebase's convention for the OPPOSITE direction (upscaling small procedural art) -- this is a ~200px crop shrinking to `ART_TILE_SIZE` (32), the same direction `TerrainRenderer._normalized_for_compositing` already established Lanczos for after nearest-neighbour aliased illustrated ground art into visible "TV static" once shrunk. Two DEPTH_BANDS-dependent constants were deliberately re-derived rather than blindly substituted: `TREAD_BANDS` is now `DEPTH_BANDS / 2.0` (was a literal `2.0` out of 4) so a full tread still packs down HALF the visible range at any band count, not 8% of it. `MAX_NEIGHBOUR_ONSET_STEP` could not stay `0.25 / DEPTH_BANDS` (a literal quarter-band): the underlying onset drift field is unchanged and its own real measured worst-case neighbour step (0.0436) does not scale down with DEPTH_BANDS, so a quarter of the new, 6x-narrower band (0.01) would fail against unchanged, correct behaviour; re-pinned to `0.05` with real margin over that unchanged measurement, reasoned as "a neighbour gap of about one of the new fine bands is still visually subtle, unlike a whole band gap was at the old coarse 4." Surfaced (not introduced) a genuine pre-existing edge case in `band_for`: at `DEPTH_BANDS=4` a maximally-lagging tile's `depth + onset_offset` at true full depth (0.82) happened to round up into the top band by coincidence (one band was wider than `ONSET_VARIANCE`); at 25 finer bands it no longer does, so `band_for` now has an explicit `depth >= 1.0` guard symmetric with its existing `depth <= 0.0` one -- once genuinely fully snowed over, onset (a lead/lag on the CLIMB to full coverage) no longer applies, so no tile is left permanently a few bands short of the top. `DUSTING_MAX_MEAN_ALPHA`/`FULL_COVER_MIN_MEAN_ALPHA` re-measured against the real sheet's least/fullest cropped cells (~0.010 / ~0.922, vs. the old procedural bands' 0.28/1.00) and re-pinned (0.06/0.80) with margin for the Lanczos resize. All 24 `test_snow_layer.gd` tests green (one obsolete, procedural-only test -- grain-block quantization -- removed, three added: `DEPTH_BANDS` pinned to the sheet's real frame count, the sheet's own measured dimensions guarded, and `build_band_image`'s output size guarded), plus all 9 snow-related `test_earth_chunk_manager.gd` tests re-run and still green with zero changes to the onset/diff-sweep spread architecture itself.

✅ **Fifth follow-up: a second, fine-grained drift layer, so a realistic local view shows real per-tile texture instead of a handful of large flat plateaus.** Reported live, after the fourth follow-up above landed: "it's not using accumulation per tile and sth like perlin noise or so instead whole areas increment to next sprite without variations." Not the old checkerboard bug (neighbours differing too much) -- closer to the opposite: `onset_offset_for`'s single broad layer (`ONSET_DRIFT_TILES = 12`) is exactly as low-frequency as the checkerboard fix demanded, which means a realistic ~20-30 tile on-screen view often sits inside one near-flat lobe of that field, where almost every tile rounds to the same band. Measured directly, not assumed: sweeping every 24x24 window across a real 400x120-tile swath of the broad-only field, the worst window found anywhere in it (tile origin `(-42, -48)`) held only 3 distinct depth bands at a mid snowfall (depth 0.5) -- pinned by the new `test_a_local_window_shows_real_per_tile_variation_not_a_uniform_plateau`, which was red against the pre-fix field for exactly that reason. `onset_offset_for` now sums TWO independent `PixelNoise.smooth` layers with distinct salts (correlated octaves of one salt can share zero-crossings, which would undercut the fix) -- the existing broad layer, and a new `ONSET_FINE_DRIFT_TILES = 2` fine layer carrying a deliberately small slice of the shared `ONSET_VARIANCE` budget (`ONSET_FINE_VARIANCE = 0.05`, with the broad share `ONSET_BROAD_VARIANCE` derived as the remainder so the two can never drift out of sync and silently blow the overall bound every other onset test depends on). The split itself was swept, not eyeballed: several broad/fine amplitude ratios and fine periods (1.5, 2, 3 tiles) were measured against the same worst-window metric; 2 tiles at a 0.13/0.05 broad/fine split gave the best real improvement (that same worst-case-anywhere window rose from 3 to 5 distinct bands) for the smallest neighbour-step cost among the periods tried. `MAX_NEIGHBOUR_ONSET_STEP` was re-measured on the combined field over the exact same sweep `test_neighbouring_tiles_have_nearly_the_same_onset` already uses (worst step 0.0357 -> 0.0612, roughly 1.53 of the current fine depth bands (0.04 each)) and re-pinned to `0.07` -- real but narrower margin than first estimated, nowhere near the old checkerboard's whole-range jump, and `test_neighbouring_tiles_have_nearly_the_same_onset`/`test_the_drift_field_still_covers_the_ground_unevenly` both re-run and still pass unchanged against the new combined field. **Correction (same day):** an independent re-verification found the originally-reported 0.0581 figure did not reproduce against the committed code -- the real, deterministically-reproducible worst step is 0.0612 (confirmed three times independently). The pinned `0.07` threshold was never wrong (0.0612 < 0.07 with real margin, so no regression existed), but the documented number was; both the code comments and this entry are corrected to the real measurement. All 26 `test_snow_layer.gd` tests green (one added), plus all 9 snow-related `test_earth_chunk_manager.gd` tests re-run and still green with zero changes to that layer's own repaint/cache architecture.

✅ **Sixth follow-up: the user replaced the illustrated sheet a second time, and this one has a genuinely different shape -- a clean 10x10 grid with an independent SHAPE-VARIANT axis, not more depth resolution.** Confirmed directly rather than assumed: `snowoverlay.png` measures 1254x1254 (was 1448x1086), an exact 10-column x 10-row grid of 125.4x125.4 cells, with NO divider-line artifacts anywhere (the same min-alpha-across-every-row/column sweep that found the old sheet's dividers finds nothing on this one). Its two axes mean two different things, confirmed by direct measurement of every cell: ROW is coverage/depth, climbing substantially and monotonically (measured mean alpha row 0 -> row 9: 0.037, 0.105, 0.126, 0.230, 0.256, 0.279, 0.303, 0.329, 0.398, 0.432) -- row 0 a tiny scattered dusting, row 9 one large puff nearly filling the cell. COLUMN is a genuinely separate hand/AI-illustrated shape VARIANT at roughly that same depth: real per-column spread exists within a row (row 0 alone ranges 0.015-0.055 across its ten columns) but does not trend column to column the way rows do -- confirmed by eye as real shape variety, not a second gradient someone forgot to sort. `SnowLayer.DEPTH_BANDS` is now `OVERLAY_ROWS` alone (10), deliberately NOT `OVERLAY_COLUMNS * OVERLAY_ROWS` (100) the way the old 5x5-all-cells-distinct sheet worked -- a real, accepted DROP from 25 depth bands to 10, since a variant is a different picture of the same depth rung, not a finer one. This trades depth granularity for something the 25-band sheet could never do at all: real per-tile shape variety at a fixed depth. `OVERLAY_BAND_CELLS`/`OVERLAY_ROW_BANDS`/`OVERLAY_COLUMN_BANDS` (the old sheet's diagonal-reading-order map and divider-avoiding crop rectangles) are deleted outright -- the new sheet needs neither, since its cells are already an exact square grid with nothing to dodge; `_cropped_cell` now just partitions the sheet by column and row directly. A new `SnowLayer.variant_for(global_x, global_y)` picks a tile's own shape (`PixelNoise.range_index`, built on `unit` -- the genuinely per-cell-INDEPENDENT form, the opposite of `onset_offset_for`'s deliberately-smooth field, since a shape choice has no coherence requirement the way a depth threshold does: two edge-adjacent tiles at the same depth SHOULD often disagree, confirmed by a new guard test finding >50% of adjacent pairs differ across an 80x8-tile sweep). `build_tile_set` now bakes a real 2D atlas, `DEPTH_BANDS * OVERLAY_COLUMNS` (100) tile images at `Vector2i(band, variant)` coordinates, and `EarthChunkManager._paint_snow_tile` computes and caches each tile's own variant the same way it already caches onset (`_snow_variant_by_tile`, cleared alongside `_snow_onset_by_tile` on chunk unload), painting `set_cell(tile, 0, Vector2i(band, variant))`. `DUSTING_MAX_MEAN_ALPHA`/`FULL_COVER_MIN_MEAN_ALPHA` re-measured against the real built (cropped + Lanczos-resized) images of every one of the ten variants at row 0 and row 9, not just one cell as before (row 0 built variants measure 0.0148-0.0554, row 9's 0.3381-0.5163) and re-pinned to 0.06/0.32 with real margin either side. `TREAD_BANDS` (`DEPTH_BANDS / 2.0`) needed no change to its formula, only its resulting value (5.0, still half of `DEPTH_BANDS`). `ONSET_VARIANCE`/`ONSET_FINE_VARIANCE`/`ONSET_BROAD_VARIANCE` needed no re-deriving at all, confirmed rather than assumed: `onset_offset_for` reads none of `DEPTH_BANDS`/`OVERLAY_COLUMNS`/`OVERLAY_ROWS`, so it is the byte-for-byte same field either way. `MAX_NEIGHBOUR_ONSET_STEP` was genuinely RE-MEASURED (not just ratio-rescaled) against the same sweep `test_neighbouring_tiles_have_nearly_the_same_onset` uses and confirmed unchanged at the real worst case 0.0612 -- expected, since it is the same unchanged field -- so the pinned `0.07` threshold stands. What DID change is how many bands that unchanged field's spread now falls across: `test_a_local_window_shows_real_per_tile_variation_not_a_uniform_plateau`'s worst-case window (same origin, same swath) dropped from 5 distinct bands to 2, a direct, expected consequence of there being fewer total bands to land in rather than any regression in the onset field's own texture -- its assertion was re-measured and moved from "more than 3" to "more than 1" (the actual bug it guards against, a whole neighbourhood locked onto a literal single band, is still caught). The two onset noise layers and the new variant axis were confirmed to solve different problems rather than overlap: onset decides which depth band a tile shows relative to the shared coverage number, variant decides which picture draws that band once chosen -- both kept. Test file substantially rewritten: `test_band_crops_stay_clear_of_the_sheets_divider_lines` (an old-sheet-only concern) deleted outright with a comment explaining why; `test_depth_bands_matches_the_illustrated_sheets_real_frame_count` renamed and re-pointed at `OVERLAY_ROWS` alone; `test_deeper_snow_is_whiter`/`test_a_dusting_lets_the_ground_show_through_and_full_cover_does_not`/`test_band_image_is_sized_for_the_atlas` swept across variants rather than pinned to column 0; four new tests cover `variant_for` (bounded, deterministic, varies across tiles, and a guard confirming neighbours disagree often rather than drifting smooth). All 29 `test_snow_layer.gd` tests green, plus a new `test_painted_snow_tiles_carry_a_real_per_tile_variant` in `test_earth_chunk_manager.gd` proving the manager actually paints the real `variant_for` value (not always column 0) and that real variety survives into the painted field, and every other snow-related `test_earth_chunk_manager.gd` test re-run and still green.

✅ **Seventh follow-up: fixed the slicer's own real artefacts (a colour halo from straight-alpha resizing, plus a ghost blob / hard clip from neighbouring cells' own paint pressing across the grid boundary), and confirmed the separately-reported "keep the initial variant so accumulation stays coherent" complaint was never a caching bug at all.** Two independent user reports this pass. The sheet had ALSO been replaced a third time by the time this landed (1536x1024, 153.6x102.4 non-square cells -- corrected from the sixth follow-up's stale 1254x1254/125.4x125.4 square figures, `test_the_overlay_sheet_has_the_measured_dimensions` re-pinned), which turned out to matter directly: a cell this much shorter (102px) than it is wide (154px) is exactly why the high-row "puff" shapes press across their own ROW boundary at substantial alpha far more than they ever press across a column one.

**The slicer artefacts.** `_cropped_cell`'s partition math was confirmed exact (gap-free, overlap-free) -- the bug was the ILLUSTRATED CONTENT, not the geometry. Two real, independently-confirmed defects: (a) a sheet-wide "colour under near-zero alpha" halo -- a real, consistent RGB persisting at alpha as low as 0.004-0.02 at real cell boundaries (e.g. row 6's column 2/3 crossing measures ~0.57/0.65/0.78 down to alpha 0.004), which `Image.resize`'s straight-alpha Lanczos blends into the kernel at FULL weight regardless of how invisible it actually is; a sheet-wide scan of all 100 built tiles found 61,204 such pixels. (b) substantial, even near-opaque, overflow from a genuinely oversized shape: `band=5,variant=2` rendered a disconnected ghost blob at the very top of its crop (unfixed top-row mean alpha 0.449, real content for that cell only starting around native row 36 -- literally a fragment of the row-4 cell above bleeding down); `band=9,variant=7` rendered a flat ~0.9 mean-alpha PLATEAU starting immediately at row 0 with no taper (that variant's real content presses UP into the row-8 cell above it, so the fixed-grid crop cannot recover the part that lives on the other side of the boundary). Fixed with two techniques together, confirmed neither alone was sufficient: `SnowLayer.build_band_image` now premultiplies alpha before the Lanczos resize and un-premultiplies after (`_premultiply_alpha`/`_unpremultiply_alpha`, guarded by `_UNPREMULTIPLY_MIN_ALPHA = 0.02` against dividing by a near-zero alpha and amplifying 8-bit quantization noise into an arbitrary colour -- measured directly: an unguarded divide produced a pure white pixel at alpha exactly 1/255 on a tile that should be nearly empty), and feathers the crop's own outer border toward transparent before that resize (`_feather_crop_edges`, `CROP_EDGE_FEATHER_PX = 8`, a smoothstep rather than linear ramp specifically because a linear ramp's kinked derivative measurably rang under the later Lanczos resize). `CROP_EDGE_FEATHER_PX` was swept from both sides (4 through 24): wide enough to matter, narrow enough that row 9 -- "one large puff nearly filling the cell," whose content already touches its own nominal edge on every one of its ten variants (measured: 0px margin on at least one side, all ten) -- keeps a real, if modest, margin over `FULL_COVER_MIN_MEAN_ALPHA` (worst variant 0.339 against the 0.32 threshold) rather than being amputated by the same fix. Both known-bad tiles' own top-row mean alpha dropped ~87% (0.449 -> 0.028, 0.915 -> 0.059); `band=9,variant=7` in particular now shows a genuine gradient instead of the unfixed flat plateau. Three new `test_snow_layer.gd` tests: a sheet-wide zero-tolerance guard for the near-invisible-colour halo (`test_no_built_tile_shows_a_strongly_coloured_pixel_at_near_zero_alpha`, red at 59,209 violations before the fix, 0 after), a guard against the two specific known-bad tiles' own top-edge signature (`test_known_bad_reference_tiles_no_longer_spike_at_their_own_top_edge`), and a guard pinning that the row-9 tradeoff was actually checked rather than assumed safe (`test_full_cover_still_clears_the_min_mean_alpha_after_the_edge_fix`). 30/32 `test_snow_layer.gd` green (2 pre-existing failures, unrelated to and unmoved by this fix, named below), plus all 11 snow-related `test_earth_chunk_manager.gd` tests re-run and still green.

**The "coherent progression" complaint was investigated, not assumed fixed by the above.** `EarthChunkManager._snow_variant_by_tile` already looked, by design, like it should keep one tile's variant fixed for its whole loaded lifetime: has()-then-compute-once against a pure function of the tile's own global coordinates (`SnowLayer.variant_for`), erased only on chunk unload and recomputed to the identical value if reloaded. A new regression test, `test_a_tiles_snow_variant_never_changes_as_depth_climbs_through_several_bands`, drives one real manager through depths 0.15/0.45/0.75/0.95 (spanning several bands) and asserts every painted tile's own atlas.y stays fixed throughout, with only atlas.x allowed to move -- GREEN on the first run (68,113 real per-cell assertions), no production change needed. The user-visible complaint was therefore very likely caused entirely by the slicer bug above: a contaminated crop at one band reading as a different SHAPE from the crop at the next band, even though the underlying variant index never moved -- visually confirmed by re-rendering the same variant across bands 2/4/6/8/9 after the slicer fix landed: a recognizably single blob thickening and growing, not a sequence of unrelated pictures.

**Two pre-existing, asset-content failures found while establishing the baseline for this pass, confirmed unrelated to and unmoved by either fix above (not fixed here, named so they are not mistaken for a regression of this work):** `test_deeper_snow_is_whiter` (row 9's real illustrated content is, in the CURRENT sheet, genuinely less white/opaque on average than row 8's -- measured on both the raw uncropped sheet and the built tiles, before touching any code in this pass) and `test_a_dusting_lets_the_ground_show_through_and_full_cover_does_not`'s dusting half (row-0 variant 7 measures 0.0659 mean alpha against a 0.06 ceiling). Both are about the sheet's real per-row CONTENT, not about cross-cell bleed or slicing, and both measured identically before and after this pass's fix (0.0659 -> 0.0658; row 9/row 8 whiteness gap unchanged) -- confirming they are not a slicer symptom, just a currently-mislabeled or under-covered pair of rows in the sheet the sixth follow-up above already flagged as freshly replaced.

✅ **Eighth follow-up: an independent re-check found the seventh follow-up's edge feather had not actually fixed either known-bad tile -- it had relabelled them -- and this pass replaces it with a connectivity-based fix that does, honestly reported as a real improvement rather than a total one.** Re-measured directly against the seventh follow-up's own committed code, not assumed from its prose: `band=5,variant=2`'s "fixed" row-0 mean alpha (0.028) was low only because the whole bleed profile had shifted down two rows, not because any of it was removed -- the feathered pipeline's row 2 (0.449) equals the UNFIXED pipeline's row 0 (0.449) almost exactly, and a full render confirmed the disconnected ghost blob was still clearly visible two rows lower. `band=9,variant=7`'s left-edge stray fragment was not addressed by the feather AT ALL (it sits well inside the crop's own left edge, outside the 8px feather zone) -- only that tile's TOP hard clip, a genuinely separate defect, was actually fixed. Also corrected: a prior free-text summary of the seventh follow-up claimed 0 violations of the near-invisible-colour guard at a looser alpha<0.05 threshold in the final committed code; re-measured directly against that exact code, the real figure is 2,104 -- the PINNED test's own alpha<0.02 threshold genuinely was, and still is, 0, so no test result was ever wrong, only an unpinned figure quoted in prose (the same kind of correction the fifth follow-up above made for its own 0.0581-vs-0.0612 neighbour-step figure).

**Why a uniform feather cannot fix this, confirmed rather than assumed.** `band=9,variant=7`'s real content already touches its own nominal cell edge with zero margin on at least one side on every one of its ten variants (re-confirmed this pass). Widening `CROP_EDGE_FEATHER_PX` enough to reach the real bleed depth (measured up to ~36 native px, more than four times the current 8px) would amputate that real, edge-touching content on row 9 rather than just the bleed -- a feather cannot tell "a neighbour's paint near this edge" from "this cell's own paint near this edge", since distance-from-edge is the only signal it has.

**The fix: connectivity, reusing `CompositeSheetSlicer`'s own technique rather than inventing a new one.** That file's own doc comment explains exactly this "blobs not gutters" reasoning for an analogous problem (telling one drawing's real content apart from a stray mark bridging into it). Adapted here for a single square cell: after cropping the nominal cell, `SnowLayer._discard_disconnected_bleed` finds every eight-connected run of painted pixels (`_connected_components`, `BLEED_COMPONENT_ALPHA = 0.3` -- swept 0.05/0.1/0.15/0.2/0.3/0.5/0.7 against both known-bad tiles' own raw crops, every value in that range gives the identical split, real margin on both sides) and, for every one that is not the cell's own dominant (largest) component, tests whether it keeps growing once the crop's own boundary is lifted by `BLEED_NEIGHBOUR_PAD_PX = 45` native px (a real neighbouring region of the same sheet, not a synthetic one; 45 measured to clear the worst real bleed depth found, ~36px, and confirmed stable by re-testing the same components at 60/77/102/120/150px of padding with no classification change). A piece of this cell's OWN content -- however many separate touching puffs it is legitimately split into (confirmed by direct render: `band=6,variant=0`'s real content genuinely IS two separate cloud clumps, not one) -- is already complete within its own nominal rectangle and does not grow when the window widens. A piece of a NEIGHBOUR's content that merely presses across the boundary keeps growing, because most of the shape it belongs to is still on the other side. A component is discarded if it grows to at least `BLEED_GROWTH_RATIO = 2.0` times its original size -- "more than half of this shape's real extent turned out to sit outside our own nominal cell," the plainest version of "this more plausibly belongs next door than here."

**`BLEED_GROWTH_RATIO` sits on a genuine continuum, not a clean gap -- measured, not eyeballed.** Sweeping every non-largest component across the real sheet, growth ratios run smoothly from 1.000 (never touches a pixel of padding -- e.g. `band=6,variant=0`'s own real second lobe, ratio 1.190) past 10 with no natural break to draw a line through: this sheet genuinely has shapes that brush their neighbours by every degree, not just "clean" or "bled." `2.0` is a deliberately conservative choice through that continuum -- it protects every measured self-contained shape found (including that same second lobe) while still catching both known-bad tiles' dominant fragments (ratios 7.47-29.25 and 11.51) and, measured as a side effect rather than targeted, a further real bleed instance elsewhere on the sheet: `band=4,variant=5` loses a 2086-native-px component (ratio 2.088) confirmed by direct render to be a genuine lobe of `band=3`'s own cloud pressing down across the row boundary -- the identical shape of defect as the two originally-named tiles, just never previously singled out.

**Honest result: substantially, not completely, fixed -- named rather than claimed clean.** `band=9,variant=7`'s left-edge fragment is now fully gone: a direct connectivity check on the crop after the discard step finds exactly 1 component (7118 native px) where there were 2 (7118 and 477). `band=5,variant=2`'s ghost blob is ~80% gone: two of its three original fragments (654 and 167 of 1024 total stray px) are removed, but the third (203px) never grows even at 150px of padding -- by this exact connectivity test it is indistinguishable from a genuine small separate puff (like `band=6,variant=0`'s own kept second lobe) and is deliberately left in place rather than guessed at. This is a named, honest limitation, not a silently missed bug.

**Measured against all 100 real tiles, not just the two known-bad ones, per this fix's own governing requirement.** Total painted mass retained sheet-wide: 88.25% (554,440 native px before `_discard_disconnected_bleed`, 489,282 after). The single worst-hit tile is `band=4,variant=5` at a 30.3% loss of its own content -- confirmed by direct render (not assumed from the number alone) to be the newly-found `band=3`-lobe bleed above, not a severed tendril of its own drawing. No other tile lost a comparably large fraction.

**Tests: the two gameable reference-tile assertions replaced, not patched, plus a new sheet-wide guard.** The prior `test_known_bad_reference_tiles_no_longer_spike_at_their_own_top_edge` checked only each known-bad tile's own row-0 mean alpha -- exactly the metric a two-row shift can satisfy without fixing anything, which is precisely what happened. Replaced by `test_known_bad_reference_tiles_have_no_substantial_stray_component` (counts connected components on the RAW crop, immediately after `_discard_disconnected_bleed` runs, at native resolution rather than the final resized tile -- a shifted row cannot fool a component count, and native resolution keeps a small survivor's real size visible rather than rounding it down to near-nothing by the later 32x32 resize: the same fragment that is 203 native px is only 11px after resize) and a companion `test_known_bad_reference_tiles_stay_clean_through_the_full_pipeline` (checks a RANGE of rows/columns on the final built tile, specifically so a future shift within that range is still caught). A new `test_bleed_removal_does_not_gut_the_sheets_own_content` pins the 88.25%-retained/30.3%-worst-loss measurements above as a real regression guard, run across all 100 tiles. `test_no_built_tile_shows_a_strongly_coloured_pixel_at_near_zero_alpha` and `test_full_cover_still_clears_the_min_mean_alpha_after_the_edge_fix` (the premultiply/colour-halo and row-9-tradeoff guards) are unchanged and still green -- both were already testing something real. 32/34 `test_snow_layer.gd` green (the same 2 pre-existing, unrelated, unmoved failures named above), plus all 15 snow-related `test_earth_chunk_manager.gd` tests re-run and still green.

✅ **Ninth follow-up: reported live again, with screenshots, after the eighth follow-up's bleed-removal fix landed -- "the snow is still broken," this time a field of deep/near-full snow rendering as an obviously artificial, grid-aligned repeating "wallpaper" of the same rounded double-lobed blob.** Investigated directly rather than assumed a regression of the eighth follow-up's own work: `SnowLayer.build_band_image(9, 0)`, `(9, 1)`, and `(9, 5)` rendered through both the CURRENT code and a reconstruction of the code from immediately before this session's two rounds of bleed-removal fixes (`git show 9471253:src/rendering/snow_layer.gd`), against the same real sheet asset, produced BYTE-IDENTICAL painted-pixel counts (395, 372, 408 respectively) -- the bleed-removal work touched zero pixels at band 9 for these variants, so this was never a regression of it. `variant_for` was independently re-confirmed to spread genuinely across a real 10x10 tile grid (all ten values present, no repetition pattern), and a duplicate-pair sweep across all 45 pairs at bands 7/8/9 found zero exact pixel duplicates -- the underlying art genuinely differs, pixel for pixel, between every one of the ten variants even at the highest bands.

What does NOT genuinely differ, visually, is the overall SILHOUETTE: row 9 -- "one large puff nearly filling the cell" (see `OVERLAY_COLUMNS`' own doc comment) -- leaves little room for shape variety across its ten hand/AI-illustrated variants, so several of them read as the same rounded double-lobed mound at a glance even though their pixels genuinely differ. The actual bug was never variant selection, band selection, or slicing: every tile painted its (genuinely similar-looking) blob in the exact same on-screen POSITION and ORIENTATION within its cell, which is what turns "several similar-looking blobs" into an obviously artificial, grid-aligned wallpaper.

**The fix is a third, independent per-tile axis.** `SnowLayer.transform_for(global_x, global_y)` is seeded off the tile's own global coordinates with its own new salt (`_TRANSFORM_SALT = 4271`, following this file's own established "each independent noise use gets its own salt" convention -- see `_VARIANT_SALT`/`_ONSET_SALT`/`_ONSET_FINE_SALT`), and returns one of four flip combinations -- identity, flip_h, flip_v, or both together -- painted directly as the `TileMapLayer.set_cell` `alternative_tile` argument. Two mirrored copies of a similar-looking blob do not read as "the same tile repeated" the way two identically-oriented copies do, even where the underlying silhouette genuinely converges at that band.

**The real Godot 4.7 API this relies on was confirmed with a minimal, direct headless test, not assumed from memory (per this fix's own governing instruction).** A throwaway `TileSetAtlasSource`/`TileMapLayer` probe (an 8x8 asymmetric image, one quadrant painted a distinct colour) confirmed a raw `TileSetAtlasSource.TRANSFORM_FLIP_H` value (4096) works directly as `set_cell`'s `alternative_tile` argument with NO `create_alternative_tile` registration call needed at all: `TileSetAtlasSource.has_alternative_tile` reports one of these values as present without it ever having been created, and calling `create_alternative_tile` with one is a no-op that returns the identical id back (`4096` in, `4096` out). A real render (non-headless, since `--headless`'s dummy rendering driver returns a null viewport texture) confirmed the pixels actually move: the marked top-left quadrant rendered at top-RIGHT once the cell's `alternative_tile` carried a raw `TRANSFORM_FLIP_H` value, with `TileData.flip_h` itself still reading `false` throughout -- the flip is applied by the renderer straight from the `alternative_tile`'s own bits, not by mutating the tile's authored data. `build_tile_set` therefore needed no changes at all -- there is nothing to register.

**Only FOUR of the full eight-member orthogonal group are used -- TRANSPOSE is deliberately excluded, checked rather than assumed safe.** Rendering real built band-9 tiles (bands 0, 3, 6, and 9, several variants each) through all four orthogonal-group members side by side showed transpose visibly distorting a wide, roughly-oval mound into a tall, narrow one. Several bands' real content is markedly NOT top/bottom symmetric -- measured directly: band 9's built tiles carry roughly 30x more alpha mass in their own top half than their bottom (variant 0: 363.7 vs 10.3; variant 5: 374.2 vs 12.5; variant 7: 369.1 vs 34.1) -- in a way a simple flip preserves (a mirrored mound is still a mound, just facing the other way) but a 90-degree axis swap does not (it turns "wide and short at the bottom" into "tall and narrow along one side," a different and visibly wrong shape rather than the same puff seen differently).

**Wired into `EarthChunkManager._paint_snow_tile` the same way onset and variant already are.** `_snow_transform_by_tile` caches each tile's own transform (a pure function of its own global coordinates) the first time that tile is painted, cleared alongside the onset/variant caches on chunk unload (`_forget_snow_paint_for_chunk`), and passed straight through as `set_cell`'s fourth `alternative_tile` argument -- `set_cell(tile, 0, Vector2i(band, variant), transform)`, where it used to rely on that argument's implicit default of `0` (identity).

**Tests, TDD throughout (red confirmed for the right reason before each green).** Five new `test_snow_layer.gd` tests: `transform_for` is bounded to the four valid combinations and never carries the `TRANSFORM_TRANSPOSE` bit, is deterministic per tile, varies across tiles, and -- the test that actually matters for this specific bug, not just the mechanism in isolation -- a real sweep finds two tiles that genuinely share the exact same `(band, variant)` pair with different transforms, and confirms their rendered pixels (after applying each one's own flip, the same way `TileMapLayer` itself does) differ, rather than pinning only that the transform ints themselves differ. A new `test_painted_snow_tiles_carry_a_real_per_tile_transform` in `test_earth_chunk_manager.gd` mirrors the existing per-tile-variant test and was run RED first (confirmed against the pre-wiring manager code: every painted cell's `alternative_tile` was still the implicit default `0` while `SnowLayer.transform_for` for those same tiles varied -- 4096/8192/12288 -- so the assertion failed for the expected reason) before the manager wiring landed and turned it green. 37/39 `test_snow_layer.gd` green (34 pre-existing plus 5 new, all 5 new ones passing; the same 2 pre-existing, unrelated, unmoved sheet-content failures named in the eighth follow-up above), plus all 17 snow-related `test_earth_chunk_manager.gd` tests re-run together (`-gunit_test_name=snow`) and still green -- 17/17, 111,872 real assertions, 566s.

✅ **Tenth follow-up: reported live, with a screenshot, after the ninth follow-up's flip-transform fix landed -- "the bigger the snow tiles get the wronger they become," alongside two unrelated near-black diamond-shaped patches visible in the same screenshot.** Both halves investigated directly, neither assumed.

**Residual cross-cell bleed at the highest bands: checked, ruled out.** The eighth follow-up's own doc comments named `BLEED_GROWTH_RATIO = 2.0` as deliberately conservative, so a live re-check was warranted rather than dismissed. Rendered all 30 real (band, variant) tiles at bands 7/8/9 -- the "bigger" tiles -- through the exact current pipeline and ran the same connected-component tooling `_discard_disconnected_bleed` itself uses: 29 of 30 tiles resolve to a single component; the one exception (`band=8,variant=4`) carries a stray fragment only 2.6% the size of its own dominant blob, far under any real flag threshold (15-20% was the bar). Bleed removal at these bands is clean -- this was not the bug.

**The real defect: `transform_for` included `TRANSFORM_FLIP_V`, and that specific flip is unsafe.** The ninth follow-up's own `TRANSFORM_TRANSPOSE` exclusion was justified by real top/bottom content asymmetry (band 9 measured ~30x top-vs-bottom), but that evidence was only ever checked against transpose -- never against `FLIP_V`, the ONE transform that inverts top and bottom. A fresh sweep of top/bottom alpha-mass ratio through `build_band_image`, every band, all 10 variants each, found real, substantial, per-band-CONSISTENT asymmetry from band 1 up (worst deviation-from-1 by band: 3.34, 6.86, 9.24, 2.53, 26.25, 9.27, 3.22, 2.38, 5.44, 69.51 for bands 0-9) -- and the DIRECTION flips partway through the ladder: bands 1-8 are bottom-heavy (a mound anchored low, tapering upward), while band 9 is dramatically TOP-heavy (up to 69.5x, worse than the ninth follow-up's own already-measured 30x), the one band whose content is known to press UP past its own cell into row 8 (see the eighth follow-up's own edge-feather discussion). `FLIP_V` inverts exactly this axis on roughly half of all painted tiles.

A rendered side-by-side of real band 7/8/9 tiles through all four transforms confirmed this is not merely a number: `FLIP_H` siblings both still read as the same coherent mound facing a different way -- exactly the "still a mound" case the transpose exclusion described -- but `FLIP_V` siblings at band 9 read as a visibly SMALLER, sparser patch floating away from the bottom of the tile with an empty gap above it, not "the same mound facing the other way." The tiles meant to show the FULLEST cover are exactly the ones a vertical flip damages most, and the damage scales with how asymmetric that band's real content is -- which is "the bigger the snow tiles get, the wronger they become" in one sentence. Left/right asymmetry was checked the same way and stayed comparatively safe to keep (worst deviation-from-1 by band: 6.43, 4.98, 3.65, 4.04, 2.59, 2.74, 2.73, 2.50, 1.95, 1.68 for bands 0-9 -- an order of magnitude milder, and consistently one direction rather than flipping), confirmed by the same rendered comparison to stay a coherent mound under `FLIP_H` at every band checked.

**Fix: `TRANSFORM_FLIP_V` and `TRANSFORM_FLIP_H|TRANSFORM_FLIP_V` dropped from `transform_for`'s combinations, leaving identity and `FLIP_H` only** -- two safe orientations instead of four, excluded for the same class of reason `TRANSPOSE` already was: a flip that inverts a shape's own real, ground-anchored orientation reads as broken, not "facing a different way." `EarthChunkManager._paint_snow_tile`/`_snow_transform_by_tile` needed no changes -- `transform_for`'s own return value is still just passed straight through.

**TDD: red confirmed for the right reason before green.** New `test_transform_never_flips_vertically` (a sweep of 4,800 tile coordinates) failed red against the pre-fix code with 2,373 of 4,800 asserts failing, every failure a genuine `TRANSFORM_FLIP_V`/`TRANSFORM_FLIP_H|TRANSFORM_FLIP_V` return value (8192 or 12288) -- confirming the defect was real and pervasive, not a corner case. Turned green by the one-line combinations-list fix above. `test_transform_is_one_of_the_four_flip_combinations_and_never_transposes` renamed to `test_transform_is_one_of_the_two_safe_flip_combinations` and its valid set narrowed to match. A new `test_band_9_content_is_severely_top_bottom_asymmetric` pins the measured >10x band-9 top/bottom ratio as a regression guard against a future re-tuning (or a future asset replacement) silently re-adding `FLIP_V` without re-checking whether it is still unsafe. Full `test_snow_layer.gd` re-run: 39/41 green -- the same 2 pre-existing, unrelated, unmoved sheet-content failures the eighth/ninth follow-ups above already named (`test_deeper_snow_is_whiter`'s band 8/9 gap, `test_a_dusting_lets_the_ground_show_through_and_full_cover_does_not`'s dusting variant 7) are still the only red, confirming this fix neither caused nor fixed them -- both are about the sheet's own row content, `transform_for` touches no pixel data at all. The two originally-fixed known-bad tiles (`band=5,variant=2`, `band=9,variant=7`) and the sheet-wide retained-mass guard (`test_bleed_removal_does_not_gut_the_sheets_own_content`) were re-run as part of the same full-file pass and are unaffected, as expected -- this fix touches only orientation, never `_discard_disconnected_bleed` or its constants.

**The two dark, near-black diamond-shaped patches in the same screenshot: investigated and ruled OUT as snow-related, not fixed here.** A pixel-level scan of every one of the 100 real (band, variant) tiles -- both the raw cropped cells and the fully built (feathered, premultiplied, resized, unpremultiplied) tiles -- for any pixel with alpha > 0.3 and value (brightness) < 0.15 found ZERO such pixels anywhere in the snow sheet. The illustrated snow art itself has no near-black, substantially-opaque content at any depth or variant. The two previously-suspected mechanisms (`_discard_disconnected_bleed`'s own discard path, and `_unpremultiply_alpha`'s low-alpha fallback) were also re-confirmed clean, as the task's own brief already expected: the discard path zeroes alpha along with colour (genuinely transparent, not opaque black), and the unpremultiply fallback only ever fires at alpha <= 0.02, staying imperceptibly translucent. Snow is definitively not the source.

The most plausible in-codebase source, based on code evidence rather than the actual screenshot pixels (which were not available to sample directly in this pass): `HillshadeShader`/`hillshade.gd` -- a genuine "translucent black overlay... painted over land," up to `MAX_SHADOW_ALPHA = 0.55`, driven by each tile's real per-tile slope/aspect data and painted over EVERY loaded ground cell (`EarthChunkManager._paint_hillshade_overlay`). This exact overlay has already been shown, this same session, to produce highly visible dark artifacts specifically near water (the 2026-08-30 "dark, grooved, static pattern over rivers" incident above was root-caused to hillshade's own near-black overlay swamping the river-flow streaks) -- and a riverbank is exactly where real terrain slope is steepest, which is exactly what pushes hillshade's alpha toward its ceiling. This is circumstantial, code-level evidence, not a confirmed identification -- flagged here as a separate, out-of-scope finding for its own investigation, not fixed as part of this pass.

✅ **Eleventh follow-up: reported live, with a screenshot, of a winter storm at deep snow -- "snow still piles only on tiles... can you make it so it seamlessly piles everywhere? without gridlines."** The screenshot showed exactly what it says: a field of separate white blobs, one per tile, each with a visible gap of bare ground to every neighbour, not a continuous blanket. This is a REAL, correct description of a real architectural limit that none of the ten follow-ups above could have touched, not a regression of any of them: every one of them (variant selection, bleed removal, the flip transform) operates entirely WITHIN one puff's own crop, and every puff on the illustrated sheet carries real, deliberate transparent padding within its own cell (`OVERLAY_COLUMNS`' own doc comment) -- so two neighbouring tiles' puffs never actually touch. No amount of cleanup inside one puff's own crop can paint anything in the gap BETWEEN two puffs, because nothing was ever painted there at all.

**The fix: a second, flat tint composited BENEATH the existing puff.** `build_band_image`'s old single-function body was split into `_build_puff_image` (the exact, unchanged illustrated-art pipeline: crop, bleed-discard, feather, premultiplied Lanczos resize, unpremultiply) and a new `_composite_base_beneath`, called in sequence by the still-public `build_band_image`. The base tint reaches every one of a tile's own four edges, closing the gap to its neighbours, while the puff continues to ride on top for real texture -- "covered, not replaced" now also protects the puff's own lumpy detail from being replaced by a flat wash underneath it.

**Design question 1: should the tint track `band` (the same quantised value the puff already uses) or the raw continuous `depth + onset_offset` ("lying") value underneath it?** The continuous value was the instinctive first answer, since re-quantising a second thing the puff's own coarse way looked like it could reintroduce a coarser version of the same gridline complaint at band boundaries between neighbours. Investigated directly rather than assumed: `build_tile_set` bakes a FIXED atlas -- one image per `(band, variant)` pair, baked exactly once, reused by every tile of that pair for the tile set's whole lifetime (see that function's own doc comment) -- and cannot express a tint that needed a genuinely unique alpha per exact tile POSITION without either an unbounded number of baked combinations or a shader-driven layer instead. This project's own `GroundTint`/`test_ground_tint.gd` already establish the real cost of that second option: "Contract tests only -- the visual result can't be asserted headless," because GUT's headless runner has no GPU pixel readback. The actual claims this fix needs to prove -- no fully-transparent seam at a real shared border; the puff stays visually distinguishable from the tint alone -- are real pixel measurements, which only the existing CPU-side `Image` pipeline can deliver in a real, deterministic, run test. `band` was the only one of the two options that could actually be verified, and it turned out to be provably safe on its own terms besides: `MAX_NEIGHBOUR_ONSET_STEP` (0.07) already sits under one band's own width (1.0 / `DEPTH_BANDS` = 0.1), so two edge-adjacent tiles' bands can never differ by more than exactly one -- confirmed by a real sweep of `band_for`/`onset_offset_for` across a real range of depths (0.05 to 1.0) and coordinates (`test_worst_realistic_neighbour_band_difference_is_at_most_one`), not derived from the arithmetic alone. Measured directly on the CURRENT (in-progress, uncommitted) sheet asset: real per-band puff mean alpha runs 0.035/0.061/0.127/0.210/0.264/0.326/0.422/0.478/0.426/0.367 for bands 0-9, and the worst real neighbour band difference across a swept 120x12-tile, 19-depth grid measured exactly 1, matching the arithmetic bound precisely.

**Design question 2: a flat, uniform-alpha rectangle would create its own new hard edge wherever two neighbours' bands differ.** `_base_edge_alpha_for_band` compresses `base_alpha_for_band`'s own interior curve toward its midpoint by `BASE_EDGE_ALPHA_COMPRESSION` (0.5) specifically at a tile's outer edge, ramping smoothstep-wise back up to the full interior value over `BASE_EDGE_FEATHER_PX` (4) pixels inward (out of `ART_TILE_SIZE` = 32) -- confirmed as a real, measured reduction against the same interior curve, not merely a differently-shaped formula (`test_base_edge_alpha_softens_the_interior_step`).

**Design question 3: does compositing a base UNDER the puff wash the puff's own texture into a flat field?** Measured as alpha standard deviation, not raw min-max range -- range is the wrong metric on purpose here, since raising the floor above 0 (closing a previously-fully-transparent gap) is this fix's own INTENDED effect, and an early version of this exact test used range and failed at bands 5 and 9 for precisely that non-reason before being corrected to stddev. Swept directly across bands 1/5/9 (variant 0) through the real pipeline: the composite/puff-only stddev ratio measures 0.889/0.799/0.720 respectively -- a real, non-trivial reduction, but nowhere near a flat wash. `BASE_TINT_MAX_ALPHA` (0.30) was chosen to sit clearly under real illustrated content's own near-opaque interior alpha (confirmed: real painted puff pixels average close to full opacity within their own shape) so a base-filled gap and a puff-covered pixel stay visually distinct. A mutation check confirmed the test is a real guard, not a tautology: setting `BASE_TINT_MIN_ALPHA`/`BASE_TINT_MAX_ALPHA` to 0.85/0.95 (near-opaque) failed it at all three bands with the composite stddev collapsing to 0.026-0.042 against a puff-only 0.169-0.456.

**Design question 4: where should this live?** Baked directly into `build_band_image`'s own output (reusing the existing `(band, variant)` atlas, `_paint_snow_tile`, and every existing per-tile cache unchanged) rather than a second `TileMapLayer`/shader painted underneath -- not assumed simpler, but the only one of the two options answerable by real, run, deterministic tests, per design question 1 above.

**`BASE_TINT_COLOR` was itself measured, not guessed.** The average RGB of every real near-opaque (alpha > 0.9) pixel sampled across all ten of the deepest band's built variants, through the real `build_band_image` pipeline, measures `(0.680, 0.745, 0.865)` -- a pale, cold blue-white -- rounded to `Color(0.68, 0.745, 0.865)` so the base tint reads as the SAME snow, not a mismatched colour peeking out from underneath it.

**Band 0 (the sheet's own dusting rung) is deliberately excluded from the tint entirely, not merely given a very small value.** `DUSTING_MAX_MEAN_ALPHA` is already pinned specifically against band 0's own measured range, precisely because a dusting is snow lying in the dips with real ground showing through, not a blanket. `base_alpha_for_band(0)` returns exactly `0.0` and `_composite_base_beneath` short-circuits explicitly at `band <= 0`, so `build_band_image(0, variant)` renders BYTE-IDENTICAL to `_build_puff_image(0, variant)` for every variant (`test_dusting_band_still_shows_real_transparent_gaps`) -- a real dusting still shows the real gaps it always has.

**Confirmed end to end, not just per-constant.** A real strip of adjacent tiles at a realistic partial snowfall (depth 0.6, real `onset_offset_for`/`band_for`/`variant_for` at real global coordinates -- the exact values `EarthChunkManager._paint_snow_tile` itself computes) was built and assembled side by side exactly as they would render in the world, across an 80-tile sweep; no fully-transparent column exists at any shared border once both sides of it are beyond the dusting band (`test_adjacent_real_tiles_show_no_transparent_seam_at_their_shared_border`). A companion per-tile invariant (`test_built_tile_has_no_fully_transparent_pixel_from_band_1_up`) checks the same claim more strongly, across all 90 real `(band >= 1, variant)` combinations individually -- a tile that individually reaches full coverage on all four of its own edges cannot leave a fully-transparent seam against ANY neighbour, whatever band that neighbour is in. A mutation check on this test (temporarily forcing `_composite_base_beneath` to always no-op) confirmed it fails loudly -- 90/90 asserts red, one per `(band, variant)` combination -- when the fix is actually absent.

**Two pre-existing, unrelated test failures, named rather than touched.** The committed `snowoverlay.png` asset is itself currently modified and uncommitted in this working tree (`git diff --stat` shows a real content change, dimensions unchanged at 1536x1024) -- almost certainly a concurrent, in-progress art pass from another session. Against the version on disk, `test_deeper_snow_is_whiter` (bands 8 and 9 are no longer whiter than the band below) and `test_a_dusting_lets_the_ground_show_through_and_full_cover_does_not` (dusting variant 7 measures 0.0658, just over `DUSTING_MAX_MEAN_ALPHA`'s 0.06) both fail -- confirmed to fail identically BEFORE any change in this follow-up (39/41 on the pre-existing suite), so this is a pre-existing, out-of-scope regression in the in-progress art, not something this fix caused or is responsible for fixing. The three tests this follow-up's own new base-tint compositing DID make newly fail against the old assertions (`test_known_bad_reference_tiles_stay_clean_through_the_full_pipeline`, `test_band_9_content_is_severely_top_bottom_asymmetric`) were re-pointed at `_build_puff_image` instead of `build_band_image`, since their real claims (bleed cleanliness; the illustrated art's own top/bottom asymmetry) are about the puff pipeline alone, not about whatever now sits underneath it by design -- both green again once re-pointed, with the reasoning for the change documented inline.

**TDD, red confirmed for the right reason before green.** Nine new `test_snow_layer.gd` tests written and added alongside the three new production constants/functions they exercise (`BASE_TINT_MIN_ALPHA`, `BASE_TINT_MAX_ALPHA`, `base_alpha_for_band`, `_base_edge_alpha_for_band`, `_build_puff_image`) -- confirmed red first as a parse error (`Cannot find member "BASE_TINT_MAX_ALPHA"`) before any of the new production code existed, then green after `_build_puff_image`/`_composite_base_beneath`/`base_alpha_for_band`/`_base_edge_alpha_for_band` landed. Full `test_snow_layer.gd`: 48/50 green (41 pre-existing plus 9 new, all 9 new passing; the same 2 pre-existing, unrelated, in-progress-asset failures named above are the only red).

✅ **Twelfth follow-up: an independent verifier re-checked the eleventh follow-up above and found the real gap it was supposed to close was only PARTIALLY closed, even though every one of its own tests passed.** Built a real 12x12 field of real tiles through the exact live pipeline (not a synthetic fixture) at a realistic partial-cover depth (0.55) and at full cover: the technical claim held (no exactly-zero-alpha pixel), but the rendered image still strongly read as a grid of separate white puffs on a visibly distinct background, not a continuous blanket -- especially between vertically-adjacent tiles and at low-to-mid depths. Reproduced directly before touching anything: a real horizontal strip of adjacent tiles at depth 0.6, rendered through the committed pipeline and visually inspected, showed exactly this -- clearly separated puffs on green, not a blanket. The eleventh follow-up's own tests were REAL, not tautological (the mutation check it ran, quoted above, genuinely proved raising the alpha ceiling would collapse its own stddev-based contrast metric) -- they simply measured a proxy ("no exactly-zero pixel", "puff stays statistically distinguishable by alpha stddev") for the real, user-facing claim ("reads as continuous coverage"), and the proxy and the real claim came apart once the actual alpha values were looked at.

**Root cause, measured rather than assumed: `BASE_TINT_MAX_ALPHA` (0.30) is a real, non-zero floor, but low enough that a base-only pixel composited over real ground still reads as tinted ground, not as snow.** Composited swatches of `BASE_TINT_COLOR` over the REAL grass green (`SeasonalFoliage.GRASSLAND_BY_SEASON["summer"]`, 0.36/0.74/0.22) at a sweep of alpha values stay green-dominant through roughly alpha 0.7, crossing to a blue-toned, snow-like mix only from there up (green/blue channels cross at ~0.72) -- 0.30 is nowhere close. The worst real composited alpha found anywhere along a real shared tile border, swept across depths 0.1-0.95 and a 30-wide coordinate range in both horizontal and vertical directions through the actual `band_for`/`onset_offset_for`/`variant_for` pipeline, measured only 0.1490 under the old constants -- a real, if unglamorous, "thin wash" rather than real coverage.

**Fix, part 1: `BASE_TINT_MIN_ALPHA`/`BASE_TINT_MAX_ALPHA` raised from 0.10/0.30 to 0.65/0.90**, chosen from the real swatch-over-grass observation above and confirmed against the worst realistic case: the same swept-border measurement with the new constants gives a worst real edge alpha of 0.7098 (band 1, the lightest non-dusting band) -- comfortably past the real green/blue crossover point. `_base_edge_alpha_for_band`'s existing compression-toward-midpoint mechanism, unchanged, turned out to help rather than hurt here: because band 1's own interior sits below the new curve's midpoint, compression pulls its edge value UP (0.65 interior -> 0.7125 edge, matching the measured 0.7098 after 8-bit quantisation) rather than down -- confirmed directly, not assumed, since the same mechanism could in principle have cut the wrong way.

**Fix, part 2: raising the alpha alone was checked directly and found to genuinely wash the puff out, exactly as the eleventh follow-up's own mutation check predicted it would.** Keeping the OLD flat-average `BASE_TINT_COLOR` (0.68/0.745/0.865) at the new 0.65/0.90 ceiling measures a real puff-vs-base luminance "pop" (puff-covered pixels' mean luminance minus base-only pixels' mean luminance, composited over the real grass colour) of only 0.0108/0.0816/-0.0027 across bands 1/5/9 -- NEGATIVE at band 9, meaning the puff would be no brighter than the plain base fill around it at the exact band meant to show the fullest, most obvious snow. Raw alpha contrast could no longer carry the puff-distinguishability claim once the floor got this high, exactly the tension the task set out to resolve rather than paper over.

**Resolution: `BASE_TINT_COLOR` moved from the puff's own flat average near-opaque tone to the mean RGB of its own DARKEST DECILE of near-opaque pixels** -- measured directly, not guessed: the near-opaque population's luminance spans 0.349-1.000 (a real bright-highlight-to-dark-shadow range in the illustrated art itself, not sampling noise), and the darkest decile's own mean is `(0.3747, 0.4706, 0.6566)`, distinctly darker and more saturated than the old average. This is not merely a number that happened to pass a contrast test -- it is the physically plausible reading too: the recessed ground between two raised puffs sits in more shadow and receives more indirect (bluer) sky light than the puffs' own sunlit surfaces, the same way real snow drifts show bluer shadows in their troughs. Re-measured with the new colour AND the new alpha together, against the same real grass, the pop rises to 0.1672/0.2813/0.2292 across bands 1/5/9 (and 0.2524/0.3455/0.2650 over `ProceduralSoilSprite.SOIL_COLOR`) -- comfortably positive everywhere. Checked against the ORIGINALLY-SHIPPED (pre-this-pass) design's own real contrast, not just against zero: that design's own worst-case pop over the same real grass is 0.0908 (thinner than the eleventh follow-up's own doc comment suggested, because that comment's own contrast numbers were never checked against a real ground colour) -- this pass's fix has a HIGHER worst case (0.1672) than the design it replaced, not merely a comparable one.

**A genuinely wrong measurement, caught and corrected within this same pass rather than shipped.** The first draft of every number above was computed against an invented "grass-like" swatch colour (0.15/0.35/0.12) rather than the actual `SeasonalFoliage` constant the game uses (0.36/0.74/0.22, notably brighter and more saturated) -- an oversight that produced a materially wrong headline claim ("the shipped design's own contrast is 0.30-0.40") that did not survive being checked against the real value. Recomputing every measurement above against the two real ground colours the codebase actually defines (`SeasonalFoliage.GRASSLAND_BY_SEASON["summer"]`, `ProceduralSoilSprite.SOIL_COLOR`) is what the doc comments and tests now cite -- named here explicitly, in the same corrective style this file's own history already uses for its own near-misses, rather than quietly fixed and left unmentioned.

**Confirmed by eye, not just by number.** Real 12x12 fields, real horizontal and vertical strips, at depths 0.3/0.55/0.75/1.0, rendered through the actual edited pipeline and composited over both real ground colours, were saved to PNG and visually inspected. At 0.55 and above the field reads as a continuous, textured blue-white/blue-grey blanket with no ground colour visible anywhere and the puffs still clearly denser/brighter than their surroundings; at 0.3 the base still shows some tile-to-tile mottling (a real, honest consequence of band quantisation at the lightest non-dusting bands, not fully eliminated), but no bare ground shows through and it no longer reads as separated blobs -- a light snowfall genuinely looking lighter than a heavy one, not a grid.

**Test suite: two tests renamed/replaced, two added, one weak-but-real test kept and annotated.** `test_adjacent_real_tiles_show_no_transparent_seam_at_their_shared_border` renamed to `..._horizontal_border` and given a `..._vertical_border` twin, since the verifier's own re-check specifically found the horizontal-only version an unexamined gap. `test_puff_detail_remains_distinguishable_over_the_base_tint` (the alpha-stddev-ratio test) replaced outright with `test_puff_visibly_pops_against_the_base_tint_once_composited_over_real_ground`, since the old metric collapses to 0.13-0.36 against the new alpha for a reason that has nothing to do with texture washing out (the base's own alpha now dominates everywhere) -- exactly the "proxy, not the real claim" failure mode this whole pass was asked not to repeat. A new `test_worst_real_tile_edge_alpha_clears_a_real_coverage_floor` replaces the old "nonzero" floor (`test_built_tile_has_no_fully_transparent_pixel_from_band_1_up`, kept in place and annotated as real-but-insufficient rather than deleted) with the real, measured-floor claim across a full realistic depth/coordinate sweep, both axes. `test_deeper_snow_is_whiter` and `test_a_dusting_lets_the_ground_show_through_and_full_cover_does_not` remain the same 2 pre-existing, unrelated, in-progress-`snowoverlay.png`-asset failures named in the eleventh follow-up -- confirmed byte-identical (dusting) or near-identical (whiteness, shifted only by the new base tint's own different contribution) before and after this pass's change, so this pass neither caused nor is responsible for fixing them.

🚧 **Snow does not lie on open water, and that guard is still pinned only by a comment.** `EarthChunkManager._paint_snow_tile`'s ocean guard is correct and deliberate -- it was audited after a live report read as a defect and is not one -- but `test_a_partial_snowfall_...` merely SKIPS ocean cells, so the guard could be deleted and the suite would stay green. A written-out characterization test (`test_snow_never_lies_on_open_water`) exists in the F8 survey and needs an owner of `tests/unit/test_earth_chunk_manager.gd` to land it.

⬜ Water freezing over is a separate, unbuilt mechanic. "Snow does not lie on water" is a deliberate boundary, not an omission -- now stated as such in `docs/concept/weather.md`.

✅ **Seeds can be picked up.** They were already real things -- drawn, and eaten by birds -- but the player could only watch them. A seed you can take is what makes deliberate planting possible: gather from a meadow, carry it, sow it where you want flowers. It joins the group the pickup sweep already reads, the same trick LiftableStone uses, and is taken from the PATCH as well as the screen so a picked seed is not still lying there for a bird to eat or the rain to root.

✅ **Flies follow a carrier.** A pack with something turned in it gets its own swarm, repositioned as the carrier moves rather than orbiting a spot on the ground. No colony and no breeding there -- nothing lays eggs in a pack that keeps moving, and a swarm bred in an inventory would be a strange thing to own. These are flies that caught the scent and stayed with it.


### Snow that never covered, and snow in spring

Both reported, both the same underlying mistake in different clothes: numbers chosen against "how long should a player watch this take" without checking the clock that actually governs them.

✅ **Snow now covers and tracks now fill.** A weather spell lasts 600 seconds. Covering was set to 2700 (four and a half spells), filling a footprint to 720 (more than one), thawing to 1800 (three) -- so a snowfall always ended long before it could cover anything, and a track cut on the first walk stayed for good. All three are expressed in WEATHER SPELLS now, with covering finishing inside one and a footprint drifting full faster than a whole field is buried. `WEATHER_PERIOD_SECONDS` moved to `WeatherModel`, where the weather lives, so there is one definition rather than a copy in whatever reads it.

✅ **It no longer snows on the blossom.** Measured the season curve instead of guessing: winter carries warmth 0.00-0.14 and the shoulder seasons run 0.15-0.85, while the freezing threshold sat at 0.25 -- well into spring. At the measured boundary, winter snows and an ordinary spring does not, while a genuinely cold climate still snows out of season because latitude scales warmth before it reaches the test.

Two of my own tests had assumed the old slow rates -- they asserted STRICTLY increasing depth over twenty minutes, which stopped holding once covering finished inside a spell. Flat at full cover is correct behaviour, not a regression; they assert non-decreasing and reaching full now.


### Every new game began on the same frozen instant, and a snowfall snapped instead of spreading

Both reported by name while actually playing, both traced to real code rather than assumed.

✅ **A new game no longer starts on a fixed frozen instant.** `_world_age_seconds` (the clock `season_at`/`warmth_modifier` are pure functions of) started at a hardcoded `0.0` for every fresh save, and was never persisted in any form at all -- not even for a loaded game. `warmth_modifier`'s own phase formula puts world-age zero at warmth **≈0.1465**, just under `Snowfall.FREEZING_WARMTH` (0.15), so every single new game began mid-winter-adjacent and reliably snowed within minutes (reported: "it starts to snow deterministically"). `EarthChunkManager.randomize_world_age()` now rolls a uniform random offset across the whole year (`NEW_GAME_WORLD_AGE_RANGE_SECONDS = SeasonCycle.SECONDS_PER_YEAR`, Godot's own default-seeded `randf()`) once, at New Game/Host Game creation, and `set_world_age_seconds` re-syncs `_last_fruiting_time`/`_snow_world_age` in the same call so the jump doesn't read as a fake elapsed span the next time fruiting or snow steps -- the exact "two clocks that have to agree" trap `jump_to_season`'s own doc comment already warns about, just at world-creation time instead of a `/season` skip. A loaded game never re-rolls: the clock is now genuinely persisted (`WorldClockPersistence`, `user://world_clock.bin`, the same `store_var` convention `PlayerSave`/`EventStorePersistence` already established) and `World._spawn_local_singleplayer_from_save` restores it **before** the first `update()` call, since chunk-loading itself reads the world age (sapling ages, ecology catchup). Verified live: 20 freshly-constructed managers landed on 20 distinct world-ages, and 40 of them spanned more than one season -- against the old code, all of them would have landed on the exact same instant, every time.

✅ **A snowfall now fills in a chunk tile by tile instead of snapping everywhere at once.** `Snowfall.accumulate`'s aggregate 0-to-1 coverage number is the right shape for the pure model, but `EarthChunkManager._paint_snow_tile` fed that SAME number to every tile in the loaded field, so the instant it crossed a depth-band boundary the whole chunk changed together in one frame (reported: "snow covers a whole chunk instantly instead of spreading progressively").
