### Weather (`concept/weather.md`)

Only real-time day/night lighting is wired into live rendering; a first deterministic weather model now exists as tested pure logic but isn't wired into the game world yet:

- **Dynamic Weather System** (large) — 🚧 Partial — `src/world/weather_model.gd` (deterministic clear/cloudy/rain/storm per region+time) is now **wired with mechanical teeth**: `EarthChunkManager.current_weather` derives the player-region weather (shown in the HUD "Season · Weather"); rain/storm **slow the player** (`weather_speed_modifier` → `Player._weather_speed_multiplier`), and wet/cold weather feeds the new **body-temperature exposure** system (see Survival). Water is now the one visibly weather-reactive surface: `weather_model.wind_strength_for` (calm on clear days, most energetic in a storm) drives `WaterShader`'s `wind_strength` uniform via `EarthChunkManager.set_wind_strength`, pacing the GPU ambient wave scroll rate to match, alongside the existing rain-ripple tie-in. Still missing: visual rain/storm particles/tint over land, combat fire-dousing, and disaster events (drought/flood/wildfire). **Divergence note (2026-08-24)**: this is currently a flat per-region hash roll, identical odds anywhere on the planet — exactly the "independent random layer" this doc's own top bullet says not to build. See the new Climate Dynamics section below, which specifies the real mechanism this is meant to become.
- **Weather Exposure Debuff** (small) — ✅ Done — cold/wet weather chills the player's warmth meter; while cold, condition (fitness) degrades faster and, while freezing, movement is slowed further (`SurvivalMeters` warmth + `Player._weather_speed_multiplier`). See Survival section.
- **Snow fills in tile by tile, not the whole field at once** (medium) — ✅ Fixed — reported: "snow still covers a percentage of a whole chunk instantly instead of gradually filling individual tiles". One lying-snow depth still drives an entire snowfall (`Snowfall.accumulate` is unchanged — one clock, one number), but every tile now leads or lags that SAME depth by its own bounded, deterministic onset offset before banding it (`SnowLayer.onset_offset_for`/`ONSET_VARIANCE`, seeded from the tile's GLOBAL coordinates), grounded in real snow settling unevenly with shelter/exposure rather than an even wash — a genuinely bare field still stays bare and a complete snowfall still reaches full cover for every tile regardless of onset; only the MIDDLE of a snowfall differs tile to tile. `EarthChunkManager._repaint_whole_field` now also gates on `SNOW_REPAINT_DEPTH_STEP` (not just a whole-band crossing), so per-tile onset variance inside a single texture band still gets several repaint checkpoints across a snowfall instead of the field sitting flat until the coarser band index finally ticks over. Two related pre-existing gaps closed as part of the same pass: a chunk streamed in mid-snowfall now gets its snow immediately (`_load_chunk` calls the new `_paint_snow_chunk` for its own tiles) rather than staying bare until the next field-wide repaint happened to cross it; and an unloaded chunk's snow tiles are already erased from the snow `TileMapLayer` on unload (`_unload_chunk`, via the same `_terrain_renderer.erase` the water/roof overlays use). **Follow-up, reported live as hard-edged white-noise SQUARES:** that per-tile onset was white noise, i.e. finer than the decision it drove — two edge-adjacent tiles measured **0.3582** apart against a **0.25** depth band, so neighbours routinely sat a whole band apart. It now samples `PixelNoise.smooth` as a drift field at `ONSET_DRIFT_TILES` (12) tiles per lift, with `MAX_NEIGHBOUR_ONSET_STEP` (a quarter band) holding touching tiles together so a band boundary takes at least four tiles to cross; pinned from both sides so nobody answers a neighbour-step failure by flattening the field. See the narrative entry above for the full mechanism, including the separate `BAND_ALPHA`/`GRAIN_BLOCK` fix that made a dusting read as frost rather than as opaque specks. **Second follow-up (2026-08-27), a THIRD report of the same symptom in the user's own words: "doesn't correctly fall and accumulate gradually on individual tiles instead after a time a whole chunk get's every tile covered."** Re-investigated from scratch rather than assumed already-fixed: a math re-derivation against the real live constants (`WEATHER_PERIOD_SECONDS=600s`, `SECONDS_TO_COVER=360s`, `ONSET_VARIANCE=0.18`, `SNOW_REPAINT_DEPTH_STEP=0.05`), a full code-path trace of every `_paint_snow_tile` call site (whole-field repaint, footprint dirty-tile repaint, and chunk stream-in via `_load_chunk`), and a test-coverage audit all independently found the mechanism itself mathematically and structurally sound: a whole-field repaint fires roughly every 18 real seconds, a band crossing spreads across 65-130 real seconds per tile's own onset lead/lag, and mixed bands are present somewhere in a loaded field for 93% of a full snowfall. The one REAL gap found: every existing "mix" test drove coverage with a single direct `set_snow_depth()` jump, never through the repeated `step_snow()` calls the real `_process` loop actually uses -- so the production code path itself had never been exercised end to end. Closed by `test_a_realistic_step_snow_driven_snowfall_paints_more_than_one_non_bare_band` (`test_earth_chunk_manager.gd`), which drives `step_snow(true, 0.0)` in small real-world-age increments up to depth ~0.55 and asserts the painted field shows more than one non-bare band. **It passed with zero production changes**, empirically confirming no logic bug survives down to the real call path. Likely explanation for the repeated report: a tuning/perception gap rather than a defect -- `DEPTH_BANDS=4` means a single tile's own visible state is still a hard four-rung ladder with no per-tile fade, and if the report came from `/ecotest`-accelerated testing (which speeds up the world clock, not covered by this investigation), every one of the real-second spread windows above would shrink proportionally and could read as instant. Worth asking directly next time this comes up: was `/ecotest` active, and does "gradual" mean the FIELD should spread out more (already true, per the numbers above) or that each INDIVIDUAL tile's own transition should visibly fade rather than hard-cut between bands (not true today, and a real, separate feature if wanted). Also found in passing, not a correctness bug: a hand-resolved merge conflict (`8c284fd`) silently dropped a once-existing per-tile diff-sweep optimization (`_snow_painted_band_by_tile`/`_sweep_chunk`) in favour of the coarser "gate + repaint everything" shape now in `main` -- every repaint still reads each tile's own onset correctly, so this cost a performance optimization, not correctness, and is left as-is rather than resurrected without a measured need. **Third follow-up (2026-08-27): that dropped optimization turned out to be the real remaining gap after all.** Re-reading the second follow-up's own numbers rather than stopping at "no logic bug survives the real call path": a whole-field repaint firing "roughly every 18 real seconds" with nothing changing in between IS the batch-pop symptom, not a clean bill of health -- individual tiles' own onset-adjusted bands cross their thresholds continuously the whole time (confirmed again this round), but between two ~18s-apart `SNOW_REPAINT_DEPTH_STEP` checkpoints not one of those crossings got painted, so every tile that crossed sometime in that whole window all repainted TOGETHER the instant the gate next fired -- "nothing happens, then a whole chunk changes at once," exactly as reported a third time. Fixed by resurrecting the dropped architecture rather than tuning the old gate further: `EarthChunkManager._paint_snow_tile` is now diff-aware (`_snow_painted_band_by_tile` tracks each loaded tile's own last-actually-painted band; a real `set_cell`/`erase_cell` only fires when a tile's freshly-computed band differs from that), and a new `_sweep_snow_field` calls it for every loaded tile on a real, MUCH tighter cadence (`SNOW_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, 2.0s, gated on world-age elapsed the same way `_snow_world_age` already is) from `step_snow`'s own per-frame call, replacing the old `SNOW_REPAINT_DEPTH_STEP`/`_repaint_whole_field` gate entirely. Recomputing each tile's onset every sweep would have made even 2s unaffordable (measured: ~200ms/pass over the real ~22,700-tile `LOAD_RADIUS=2` field, before touching the tile layer at all) -- fixed by caching onset per tile the first time it's painted (`_snow_onset_by_tile`, a pure function of the tile's global coordinates that never changes for its loaded lifetime, cleared on chunk unload), which cut the same sweep to ~40-50ms. That keeps the new mechanism's average CPU cost roughly the SAME order as the old one's (~45ms every 2s vs. the old unconditional repaint's ~426ms every 18s measured live -- ~2.1% vs. ~2.4% of wall-clock time) while making it 9x more frequent, so a real crossing shows up within ~2s instead of sitting invisible for up to 18s and then jumping. Driven by a new failing-first test, `test_step_snow_driven_coverage_changes_trickle_in_rather_than_batching_every_18_seconds` (`test_earth_chunk_manager.gd`): confirmed RED against the unmodified gate (checkpoints ~19s apart, matching the derived old cadence almost exactly), GREEN after the fix. The test's own sample had to be a STRIDED spread across the whole loaded 5x5-chunk field rather than one compact on-screen box -- a compact box sampled mostly-correlated onset (the drift field is deliberately low-frequency, `ONSET_DRIFT_TILES`=12) and showed a real but coincidental ~20s local quiet patch even with the fix in place, which is expected spatial clustering, not a mechanism failure. All 9 existing snow tests (`test_snow_layer.gd` 22/22, every snow test in `test_earth_chunk_manager.gd`) still pass unmodified. `SNOW_REPAINT_DEPTH_STEP` and the aggregate `_snow_painted_band`/`_snow_painted_depth` fields are gone, fully subsumed by the per-tile dictionary. **Superseded (2026-09-03):** the whole `SnowLayer`/per-tile-band mechanism this bullet describes was deleted outright by the GPU texture-bombing rewrite (`snow_bomb_shader.gd`, `snow_stamp_atlas.gd` — `snow_layer.gd` and `test_snow_layer.gd` removed, not deprecated); coverage is now a continuous per-pixel shader read, not a banded tile paint. This bullet is left as historical record of the mechanism that shipped and was fixed three times over, rather than rewritten, since a full rewrite of this section is out of scope for the pass that found this (see the regression noted immediately below, found while verifying an unrelated mechanism).
- **Regression: a dangling `preload` of the deleted `snow_layer.gd`** (small) — ✅ Fixed (2026-09-03) — the GPU rewrite above deleted `snow_layer.gd` but missed one remaining consumer: `src/rendering/procedural_tree_sprite.gd`'s canopy snow-level quantization (`SNOW_LEVELS := SnowLayer.DEPTH_BANDS`) still `preload`ed the now-gone file, which broke *loading that script* — and therefore `Player`/`CharacterView`/every creature and tree renderer that depends on it, i.e. most of the game — for anyone running the test suite or launching the game itself. Found while adding a wiring test for an unrelated mechanism (see the Fishing section) that instantiates `Player` and hit the parse error immediately. Fixed by giving `SNOW_LEVELS` its own pinned constant (same value, 10, that `SnowLayer.DEPTH_BANDS` last exposed) instead of reading a file that no longer exists — same quantization behaviour as before, just no more dangling dependency. Pinned by `test_snow_level_is_quantized_to_ten_bands` (`test_procedural_tree_sprite.gd`), confirmed red (script failed to parse/load) before the fix and green (28/28) after.
- **Weather feeds creature behaviour** (small) — ✅ Done (one hook) — weather had gameplay teeth for the player (above) and for the soil (`soil_moisture` → earthworms → robins, see Soil Fauna section) well before it touched anything an animal actively *does*. `GrazerForaging.snowing` (new instance field, default `false`) scales `GRAZE_SECONDS` — the head-down graze bout only, not `REGRAZE_SECONDS` or `APPROACH_TIMEOUT` — by a new tuned `SNOW_GRAZE_MULTIPLIER` (1.5×) while snow is actively falling: a grazer has to paw/crater through what's landing on a tuft to keep its muzzle in it, a real winter-foraging cost. The swallow point (`SWALLOW_FRACTION`) now derives from the *current* (possibly scaled) phase duration rather than the raw clear-weather constant, so a snowy bout is uniformly slower throughout rather than fast-to-reach-the-food-then-idle. `EarthChunkManager.is_snowing()` (new) caches and exposes the same per-frame active-precipitation boolean `step_snow` already computes accumulation against, so a second reader can't disagree with what the ground is accumulating; `CreatureMarker._process` reads it the same defensively-guarded (`has_method`) way it already reads `ambient_warmth` and pushes it onto its own `GrazerForaging` instance once a frame. Tested at all three layers: pure logic (`test_grazer_foraging.gd`, 5 new tests — a bout run under two weather states from an identical start finishes on schedule when clear and is measurably still going when snowing, pinned to the exact scaled threshold from both sides), the manager (`test_earth_chunk_manager.gd`, 2 new tests), and the fully-wired creature (`test_creature_marker.gd`, 1 new test — two otherwise-identical hungry horses given the same visible tuft, one clear one snowing, diverge measurably: the snowing one has not yet taken its first bite at the exact frame count the clear one already finished at, then does still feed given a further budget — slower, not stuck). See `concept/weather.md`'s new "Weather feeds creature behaviour" section for the full mechanism and real-world grounding, cross-linked from `concept/ecosystem_dynamics.md`'s "Grazing is an act, not an aura". **Deliberately scoped to one hook**: `ThreatAvoidantWander`'s effective sensing radius shrinking in falling snow (reduced visibility, same family as Fog Line-of-Sight Reduction below) and a genuine shelter-seeking drive on `CreatureNeeds` (the world has no queryable shelter/den concept yet) are both named as real, plausible, un-built follow-ups in `concept/weather.md`'s own open questions rather than attempted here.
- **Seasonal ground cover (grass tint, tall grass, crop tops)** (medium) — ✅ Done — built, tested and wired. `src/rendering/seasonal_foliage.gd` is the ground-cover analogue of `IllustratedTree`'s canopy-frame table: what a season multiplies living green by, blended across a turn by the same `SeasonTransition.state_at` the canopies already turn on, so the lawn and the crown above it cannot disagree about the month. Each season names a real target colour for a grassland tile and the multiplier is that target divided by summer's, so summer is the identity by construction and high summer stays pixel-for-pixel what shipped. A greenness gate (`GREENNESS_GAIN`, measured against the real biome palette: every green biome ≥0.85, every non-green one exactly 0) keeps one whole-terrain material from browning the ocean and the desert in autumn, and the GLSL in `GroundTint`/`IllustratedGrassPatch` is the same expression with that constant interpolated in, so the tested GDScript and the running GLSL cannot drift. A tint, deliberately not four sets of art — baking the season would mean four ~5MB atlas bakes and a full `TileSet` rebuild landing mid-session at the exact moment the season turned. The sending half landed in the same programme: `EarthChunkManager.set_season_tint` fans the live tint onto every green thing the manager owns (the same shape as `set_wind_strength`/`set_sun_position`), and `World._client_process` pushes `SeasonalFoliage.tint_for_world_age(world_age_seconds())` into both the ground material and that fan-out once a frame, immediately after `set_sun_position` — read off the same world clock every other season reader uses, so the lawn and the canopy cannot disagree about the month. Wiring pinned by `tests/unit/test_world_season_fanout.gd` (6/6). Confirmed live: an autumn world renders a muted olive-brown lawn under autumn canopies, where it previously stayed high-summer green.
- **The season cannot go stale in either cache** (small) — ✅ Done — there are TWO caches between the painted pixels and the screen and the season has to stay out of both. The disk atlas is keyed by `ATLAS_VERSION` (the season is never baked — `grep` confirms it appears nowhere in `terrain_renderer.gd`/`procedural_terrain_sprite.gd`/`terrain_atlas_cache.gd` — pinned by `test_the_season_never_enters_the_atlas_cache_key_so_a_cached_atlas_cannot_go_stale`). The built `TileSet` is then memoized process-wide by `TerrainRenderer._tile_set_cache_key`, a *separate* key added by the boot-time performance pass that the first guard is blind to: a season folded into it would rebuild all 10,240 atlas cells mid-session without ever touching `ATLAS_VERSION`. `test_a_season_turn_changes_the_material_and_not_one_pixel_of_the_atlas` covers that second key behaviourally — a turn to winter must land on the *material* while the memoized `TileSet` and the baked grassland tile's pixels come back identical. Verified by mutation rather than by a fabricated red: adding the live season to `_tile_set_cache_key` makes it fail immediately, while the older `ATLAS_VERSION` guard still passes.
- **Seasons (calendar cycle)** (medium) — ✅ Done — `src/world/season_cycle.gd` (tested, see `concept/seasons.md`): a deterministic spring→summer→autumn→winter year with smooth warmth/growth modifiers. Wired into fruit phenology (`EarthChunkManager._warmth_at_pixel` scales `FruitingModel` warmth by season, so trees fruit fast in summer / slowly in winter) and shown in the HUD. A new world now starts at a random point in the year rather than always on the same frozen instant, and a loaded world resumes its own persisted point rather than re-rolling (`randomize_world_age`/`load_world_clock`, `WorldClockPersistence` — see `concept/seasons.md`'s "A new world starts at a random point in the year"). **`growth_modifier` now drives vegetation growth too (2026-08-26)** — it existed with zero live callers until this pass; `EarthChunkManager` computes it once per step from `_world_age_seconds` and threads it through as an extra `advance(delta, growth_modifier)` argument on every per-chunk patch sim's growth increment (`TallGrass`, `WildCropPatch` — keeping its own pinned ratio to `TallGrass.GROWTH_RATE` intact, both scale by the same modifier — `FlowerPatch`'s seedling growth only, not its unrelated nectar/seed regen, `DesertScrub`, `TundraLichen`). Spread timing is untouched by design; only the growth increment scales, with a raised floor (0.2) so nothing fully stops growing even at winter's trough. Still not wired: farming crop viability (`farm_plot.gd`'s player-planted crops, a separate system from the wild carrot/potato patches above).
- **Regional Weather Variety** (medium) — 🚧 Partial — `weather_model.gd` takes a `region_seed` parameter so different regions roll independently; not wired to any real per-chunk region concept yet.

### Evolution (`concept/evolution.md`)

No genetics reaches a living animal: an offspring inherits its species string and nothing else (`CreatureRenderer.spawn_single`, `src/rendering/creature_renderer.gd:263`, rolls a fresh `randi()` wander seed on `:266`, and that seed is exactly what `CreatureInfo` derives level and max_health from, `src/world/creature_info.gd:351-353`). Three pieces of the machinery are nonetheless real, tested and **unwired** -- marked 🚧 individually below, not ⬜ -- and DNA does exist elsewhere in the tree for trees (`TreeGenome`) and for character creation (`HeroDna`).
